title: Registry payload: three command descriptions still promise a boundary test run
action: Found by the tdt-1 judge as the same defect in a different file. Three command descriptions in the registry payload still state the retired boundary auto-run, and they are USER-VISIBLE twice over: they are the MCP tool descriptions clients read, and the text `bee <command> --help` prints. (1) `cells.cap` and (2) `cells.finish` both carry 'Tests prove at the boundary — `bee close` runs commands.test when the feature has no worktree, `bee worktree merge` runs it when it does; CI runs the same command on every push', plus a sentence saying a repo with commands.test declared records {tests: 'boundary'} on the trace. The first half is false: decisions 58ec9664/1f534837 retired the boundary run — each cap records its own proof line, both doors call feature_proof_check and run nothing, and CI is the only thing that runs the command. The trace sentence needs care rather than deletion: handlers_close.rs still WRITES the literal "boundary" as a legacy sentinel that no door reads, so describe it as the legacy value it is, do not claim it was removed. (3) `cells.reopen` says the reopened cell goes 'back through the full finish door — including the declared commands.test run'; there is no such run. Rewrite all three to state the live rule. Keep each description's surrounding sentences, its shape, and its length discipline — these are reference text, not prose. NOTE ON SCOPE: this file is a generated artifact and is hook-guarded; catalog.rs reads its rows (that is the pinned-count pair the active pattern docs/knowledge/patterns/20260818-a-generated-view-in-scope-puts-its-source-record-in-scope.md describes). No .rs file carries these strings, so the payload IS the record here. If the write guard denies the edit, follow the remedy it names and report which path it required. Run `bee dev regen` after the edit and include anything it rewrites.

truths: `bee cells cap --help`, `bee cells finish --help` and `bee cells reopen --help` no longer say any local door runs commands.test.
The same three descriptions in the registry payload state the live rule: each cap records its own proof line, the doors check that record, CI runs the command on every push.
The trace sentence describes `boundary` as the legacy value the cap still writes and no door reads — it does not claim the value was removed, because handlers_close.rs still writes it.
`bee dev regen` runs green afterwards and anything it rewrites is included in the same commit.
The full suite is green, including whatever pinned-count test guards this payload.

done_when: The three descriptions state the live proof-line rule, regen is green, and the full suite passes.
notes: Disjoint from tdt-3, which sweeps the docs. Do not touch docs/ in this cell.
